title: The AI Guard HookProvider for Strands Agents: which hook events it uses, how each leg can block, and what stays out of reach

prose.text: The Strands integration is one HookProvider passed to the agent; each leg's enforcement is limited by what the Strands event for that leg lets a hook write. {{hook-events}}

prose.label: Tools.
prose.text: {{tool-input-cancel}} {{tool-output-replace}} {{side-effects}} The tool event is sent as text, as in the AgentCore guard: [[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.aws-bedrock-agentcore:tool-event-serialized]], with the README disagreement in [[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.aws-bedrock-agentcore:tool-event-shape]].

prose.label: Options.
prose.text: {{constructor-options}} The README names an option the class lacks {{divergence:scan-tool-input}}. {{readme-invalid-python}} {{async-executor}} Shared behavior, including the 10-second timeout that ignores AIGUARD_TIMEOUT, is in [[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.aws]].

hook-events.statement: `AIGuardHooks` registers callbacks on BeforeInvocationEvent (which only resets the response retry budget), BeforeModelCallEvent, AfterModelCallEvent, BeforeToolCallEvent and AfterToolCallEvent.

quotes: A fifth callback on BeforeInvocationEvent scans nothing: it resets the
response-leg retry budget so one invocation cannot spend the next one's.

of every invocation, so the budget is cleared here as well as on the
        # response leg's own exits. It scans nothing

prompt-leg.statement: Before each model call the provider scans the system prompt plus every user-role message it has not yet scanned (tracked by each message's `tracking_id`) and blocks by setting `cancel`, so the model is not called; a blocked turn is remembered and keeps cancelling, without a new scan, until it is removed from `agent.messages`.

quotes: note="blocked user turn still in history")
# still reach the model, so the leg cancels again -- without a scan.
Drop the turn from `agent.messages` (or start a new conversation) to clear it;
the system prompt plus every user-role message not yet scanned

opaque-model-legs.statement: Content that cannot be read as text (a document, image or video block, encrypted reasoning, or any block type the framework adds later) is checked before the text: when `on_unscannable` is `"block"` (the default) it cancels the prompt leg, and on the response leg it raises `AIGuardResponseBlocked` at once, without retrying.

quotes: # Document/image/video in the model's own turn cannot be inspected
# as text, and this event cannot substitute. Fail closed without
# retrying -- the same shape would come back and loop.
It is checked *before* the text, so a mixed `[{text}, {document}]` turn fails closed instead of being scanned on its text alone

*everything else* is treated as unreadable -- a document, image or video block, encrypted (`redactedContent`) reasoning, a tool-result member this file does not recognise, and any block type the framework adds after this file was written
the prompt leg cancels the model call, the response leg raises `AIGuardResponseBlocked`, and the tool-output leg replaces the result

response-retry.statement: AfterModelCallEvent lets a hook write only `retry`, so a blocked response is discarded and the model is called again, up to `retry_limit` (default 2) per invocation; after that the provider raises `AIGuardResponseBlocked`.

quotes: (`AfterModelCallEvent` permits writing only `retry`). A blocked response is
therefore discarded and the model is called again, up to `retry_limit`;
# The response-leg retry budget is per invocation

stream-before-verdict.statement: Strands streams tokens to the agent's callback handler as the model produces them, so a stream consumer may already have received a response's tokens when the response leg discards it; the README quotes the Strands SDK's own note to that effect.

quotes: *"streaming events from the discarded response will have already been emitted to callers before the retry occurs."*
The response leg detects and can terminate; it cannot guarantee a user never saw the content.
Strands streams tokens to the agent's callback handler (the default `PrintingCallbackHandler` prints them) as the model produces them

retry-scan-count.statement: A response retry re-enters the model-call loop at BeforeModelCallEvent and repeats both scans, so with `retry_limit=2` and a response that stays blocked one invocation issues six scans.

quotes: A response retry repeats **both** the prompt and the response scan, because `event.retry` re-enters the model-call loop at `BeforeModelCallEvent`:
with `retry_limit=2` and a response that stays blocked, one invocation issues six scans, not four.

tool-input-cancel.statement: A blocked tool input sets `cancel_tool`, so the tool does not run.

tool-output-replace.statement: A blocked tool output, or one carrying a member other than `text` or `json` when `on_unscannable` is `"block"` (the default), is replaced by an error tool result whose text is the block reason, so it never re-enters the model.

quotes: The member list is an allowlist: `text` and `json` are the two text-bearing

# Block: AfterToolCallEvent CAN substitute -- replace the result so the
        # poisoned / leaking output never re-enters the model.

side-effects.statement: By the after-tool leg a tool's side effect has already happened; that leg protects the model from the result, and the README points to scanning the tool's input (the before-tool leg) to gate the call itself.

quotes: a tool's *side effect* has already happened by the after-tool leg -- that leg protects the model from the result, not the outside world from the tool.
Scan a tool's input (before-tool) to gate the call itself.

structured-output.statement: `Agent.structured_output()` and `structured_output_async()` call the model outside the agent loop, fire neither model-call event, and so reach the model unscanned; the README points to `agent(prompt, structured_output_model=MyModel)`, which runs through the loop.

quotes: which runs through the agent loop and **is** scanned -- use that form.
Both methods are deprecated in favour of `agent(prompt, structured_output_model=MyModel)`

seeded-history.statement: In a caller-supplied history, assistant-role turns are not scanned and a `toolResult` block inside a seeded user turn is not walked.

quotes: assistant-role turns in such a history are not scanned
a `toolResult` block inside a seeded user turn is not walked

constructor-options.statement: The constructor takes `app_name`, `policy_id`, `session_id`, `app_user`, `ai_model`, `agent_arn`, `agent_id`, `agent_version`, `on_error`, `on_unscannable`, `strict_verdict`, `on_verdict`, `retry_limit`, `tool_server` (default `strands-tools`) and `timeout`; it has no option to turn off the tool-input leg.

readme-invalid-python.statement: The README's configuration example has two bare `policy_id=` lines, so it is not valid Python as written; one calls the value an "AI profile UUID", while the module parses the policy ID with int().

async-executor.statement: The callbacks are coroutines that hand the blocking scan to the running event loop's default executor; the leg still waits for the verdict, but other sessions on the loop keep running.

scan-tool-input.summary: Whether the Strands provider can turn off the tool-input leg.

positions.says: The README's Limitations advise setting scan_tool_input=False to keep only the output leg when the source-code detector blocks benign tool input.

quotes: or set `scan_tool_input=False` and keep the output leg.

positions.says: The constructor has no scan_tool_input parameter.

scan-tool-input.impact: Passing scan_tool_input raises TypeError for an unexpected keyword; the remaining workaround is a policy profile without the source-code detector.
